experiment: yolo26 width-0.375 intermediate size, official COCO stage
question: can an intermediate model size, trained properly, beat the n/s/m/l/x scaling curve?

init.method: ChannelPlan slice at w=0.75 with importance-sorted channels
init.head: reinitialised for nc=80 (365 -> 80), as the official pipeline does
init.note: no Objects365 checkpoint exists at width 0.375, so that stage was inherited by slicing rather than trained

recipe.source: verbatim from yolo26s.pt train_args (the official COCO stage for size s)

comparison.verdict: Pareto-DOMINATED by yolo26n: lower mAP at 2.2x the parameters

interpretation.established: slicing yolo26s down to width 0.375 and fine-tuning 70 epochs does NOT produce a competitive model
interpretation.NOT_established: that intermediate widths are worthless as architectures
interpretation.reasoning: landing BELOW n is the tell. A width-0.375 architecture with a true 150-epoch Objects365 pretrain should comfortably beat n given 2.2x the capacity. Scoring under n points at the INITIALISATION as the binding constraint, not the architecture -- consistent with this study's earlier finding that sliced-init sub-nets start near zero and recover only partially.
interpretation.clean_test_not_run: true from-scratch arms at matched budget (~60-90h GPU)
